Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
LOWELL SCHOOL COMMITTEE 
REGULAR MEETING MINUTES 
, 2025 
 
 
 
 
 
Date: October 7, 2026 
Time: 6:30PM 
Location: City Council Chamber, 375 Merrimack Street, 2nd Floor, Lowell, MA 01852 
____________________________________________________________________________________ 
Members of the public can view the meeting via LTC.  Those wishing to speak about a specific agenda 
item must register in advance by emailing the Superintendent.  Please include the agenda item, as well 
as your phone number and email address so we can provide a Zoom link for access. The email address is 
skeo@lowell.k12.ma.us. If you do not have access to email, you may contact us at 978-674-4324. All 
requests must be submitted by 2:00 p.m. on the day of the meeting. 
 
1. SALUTE TO FLAG 
 
2. ROLL CALL 
 
On a roll call at 6:31 p.m., members present were, namely: Mr. Lay, Ms. McFadden, Mr. Bahou, Mr. 
Conway, Ms. Delrossi and Mayor Gitschier. Ms. Martin was absent. 
 
3. SPECIAL ORDER OF BUSINESS 
 
3.1. Spotlight On Excellence: Morey Elementary School "School of Recognition" for 2026 
 
The Spotlight on Excellence featured Morey Elementary School, which was named a “School of 
Recognition” for 2026. Ms. McLaughlin, Principal of Morey Elementary School, addressed the 
Committee and expressed her appreciation for their continued support. She noted that the recognition 
is a reflection of the dedication and hard work of the school’s staff and students, who she said deserve 
the credit for this achievement. Ms. McLaughlin also shared several brief statements from students 
highlighting their positive attitudes and pride in the Morey School community. 
 
3.2. Superintendent's Evaluation 
The End-of-Cycle Summative Evaluation Report assessed the Superintendent’s performance in three 
goal areas: (1) professional practice, (2) student learning, and (3) district improvement. The report also 
evaluated performance across four standards: (1) instructional leadership, (2) management and 
operations, (3) family and community engagement, and (4) professional culture. 
Goal progress was rated on a five-point scale: Did Not Meet the Goal, Some Progress, Significant 
Progress, Met Goals, and Exceeded Goals. Performance on the four standards was rated on a four-point 
scale: Unsatisfactory, Needs Improvement, Proficient, and Exemplary. The Superintendent’s overall 
summative rating was Proficient.
(Page 2 of 7) 
 
Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
 
Mayor Gitschier moved to enter into discussion with the Superintendent regarding his current 
contract and possible extension of said contract; the motion was seconded by Ms. McFadden. The 
motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to accept and to place this on file as a report of progress and to rate the 
Superintendent’s overall Summative Performance as Proficient; the motion was seconded by Ms. 
Delrossi. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent. (Ms. Martin). 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to suspend the rules to take agenda item 6.4 out of order; the motion was 
seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
4. MINUTES 
 
4.1. The Approval of the Minutes of the Regularly Scheduled Lowell School Committee Meeting of 
September 16, 2026. 
 
Ms. Delrossi moved to accept and place on file the minutes of the Regularly Scheduled School 
Committee meeting that was held on September 16, 2026; the motion was seconded by Ms. 
McFadden. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
5. PERMISSION TO ENTER 
 
5.1. Permission to Enter – October 7, 2026 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to approve the Permission to Enter; the motion was seconded by Ms. Delrossi. The 
motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
6. MOTIONS 
 
6.1. [By Danielle McFadden]: Request the Superintendent or designee, explore the feasibility of 
identifying a centralized location where Lowell Public Schools facilities operations could be housed in a 
single location, including administrative offices, equipment, materials and storage, and report back to 
the School Committee on potential locations (including the Ste. Jeanne D’Arc School), operational 
efficiencies and cost considerations. 
 
Ms. McFadden moved to approve; the motion was seconded by Mr. Bahou. The motion passed with 6 
yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
6.2. [By Eileen DelRossi]: Request the superintendent to research the 2013 financial literacy funding 
given to Public Schools to breakdown where and how it was dispersed and update where we stand with 
the new state legislation on financial literacy in all of our schools in the district. 
Mr. Patel registered to speak on this motion and urged the Committee to support the request and spoke 
about the importance of it. 
Ms. Delrossi moved to approve; the motion was seconded by Mr. Bahou. The motion passed with 6 
yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin).
(Page 3 of 7) 
 
Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
 
 
6.3. [By Eileen DelRossi]: Request the superintendent to have the traffic engineer monitor the traffic 
being held back on beacon street from 9:05 to 9:30am and again at the Robinson School dismissal 
between 2:05 and 2:25pm. There is also a need for clearer signage or a trained crossing guard during 
these heavy traffic times. 
 
Mayor Gitschier stated that he will file this motion with the City Council. 
 
Ms. Delrossi moved to approve; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 
1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
6.4. [By Fred Bahou]: Motion to fully fund remainder of transportation costs of $8000 to the AFJROTC 
program for academic year 2026-2027 obligations the program must attend to maintain designation. 
The monies can be transferred from the transportation budget or where Superintendent sees as the 
most appropriate option. 
Ms. Siek and Mr. Murray both registered to speak on this motion and urged the Committee to support 
the request. They also spoke about their experiences in the ROTC program. 
Mayor Gitschier requested that a report be provided to the Committee detailing the costs associated 
with the ROTC program for each of the past three years. 
Mr. Bahou moved to approve; the motion was seconded by Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 
absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
Ms. Delrossi moved to suspend the rules to take agenda item 6.2 out of order; the motion was 
seconded by Mr. Conway. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
7. REPORTS OF THE SUPERINTENDENT 
 
7.1. 2026 Assessment and Accountability Reporting 
 
Ms. Crocker-Roberge, Assistant Superintendent of Schools & Leadership, presented the Committee with 
a report on the accountability data released by the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education 
(DESE) on September 22, 2026. The data included 2026 MCAS and ACCESS achievement and growth 
results, attendance and chronic absenteeism rates, four-year and extended graduation rates, annual 
dropout rates, and advanced coursework completion rates. In 2026, schools maintained their 2025 
accountability classifications, reflecting greater overall consistency compared with the years 
immediately following the pandemic. 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 7.1 and 7.5 as reports of 
progress; the motion was seconded by Ms. McFadden. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. 
Martin).
(Page 4 of 7) 
 
Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
 
7.2. Response to Motion (By Dominik Lay 09/02/2026) Regarding Ensuring a Smooth Opening Day 
 
Superintendent Skinner provided the Committee with an update on the successful opening of the 2026-
2027 school year at Lowell Public Schools. Staff returned on August 31st, students in grades 1-12 
returned on September 2nd, and Pre-K and Kindergarten students began on September 8th. The opening 
of the school year was smooth and orderly, reflecting the extensive preparation and coordination 
among school-based staff, district departments, and city partners. 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 7.1 and 7.5 as reports of 
progress; the motion was seconded by Ms. McFadden. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. 
Martin). 
 
7.3. HVAC Systems Update 
Dr. Hall, Assistant Superintendent of HR & Operations, provided the Committee with an update on HVAC 
system inspections and preventative maintenance across the district. He reported that he had contacted 
the Department of Public Works (DPW) in early September to request that all school HVAC systems be 
tested. Dr. Hall also noted that the Mayor had requested that the DPW complete these inspections, as 
discussed during a City Council meeting. The DPW recently confirmed that contractors had been 
performing preventative maintenance on boilers throughout the district’s schools. No major issues were 
reported. However, adjustments were being made at Stoklosa Middle School, and McAuliffe Elementary 
School is waiting on the delivery of parts needed to repair its temperature controls. Both issues were 
expected to be resolved by the end of the following week. 
Mr. Bahou moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 7.1 and 7.5 as reports of 
progress; the motion was seconded by Ms. McFadden. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. 
Martin). 
 
7.4. Finance Updates 
Dr. Pinto, Assistant Superintendent of Finance, provided the Committee with a financial update outlining 
the department’s ongoing efforts to monitor Fiscal Year 2027 (FY27) and begin planning for Fiscal Year 
2028 (FY28). The Finance Office is reviewing the district’s enrollment verification, a critical component of 
the state funding formula used to calculate Chapter 70 funding. The End-of-Year Reporting (EOYR) 
process is also underway. The City Finance Department submitted the Maintenance of Effort (MOE) 
report on September 17th, which the Finance Office is currently reviewing. The department has 
requested confirmation and supporting documentation for several items, including painting materials, 
School Resource Officer salaries, and crossing guard expenses. Lowell Public Schools received an 
extension from the Department of Elementary and Secondary Education (DESE) to submit the EOYR by 
October 31, allowing additional time for Committee review of the City’s MOE report. The Finance Office 
has also begun its first round of FY27 budget meetings with school principals. These meetings include 
reviewing budget and funding pages in principals’ workbooks, examining ledgers to support expense 
tracking, introducing an updated position control system, and addressing budget-related questions.
(Page 5 of 7) 
 
Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
 
Additionally, United Teachers of Lowell (UTL) representatives received information on September 15 
and September 17th regarding the teacher pay schedule. At the beginning of the school year, the City 
agreed to issue teacher payments ahead of schedule, resulting in two full paychecks being issued on 
September 10th and September 17th. Consequently, the gap between the final paycheck in August and 
the start of the school-year pay schedule in September 2027 is expected to recur. UTL representatives 
are scheduled to meet with the City Auditor’s Office in the coming weeks to explore potential solutions. 
Mr. Bahou moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 7.1 and 7.5 as reports of 
progress; the motion was seconded by Ms. McFadden. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. 
Martin). 
 
7.5. Personnel Report 
 
The Personnel Report officially informs the Committee of all retirements, resignations, promotions and 
new hires.  
 
Mr. Bahou moved to accept the following Reports of the Superintendent 7.1 and 7.5 as reports of 
progress; the motion was seconded by Ms. McFadden. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. 
Martin). 
 
7.6. Home Education 
 
Superintendent Skinner recommended that the following parents/guardians be allowed to home 
educate their child:  
Melissa Alamed 
Rosemond Konadu 
Yarixza Munoz 
Naina Avanesova 
Silvia Chevalier 
Amanda Bettencourt 
Thomas Dyer 
Sean Gibney 
 
Mr. Lay moved to approve Home Education; the motion was seconded by Ms. Delrossi. The motion 
passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
8. NEW BUSINESS 
 
8.1. Approval to Accept and Expend Allocated FY27 Award 
 
These grant funds have been secured by the Lowell Public Schools through the Opioid Abatement 
Funding for iDECIDE Program. 
 
Mr. Conway to approve, accept and expend the allocated FY27 awards; the motion was seconded by 
Mr. Bahou. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin).
(Page 6 of 7) 
 
Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
 
 
8.2. Budget Modification Request 
 
Mr. Lay moved to approve the budget modification in the amount of $3,600; the motion was 
seconded by Ms. Delrossi. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
8.3. Budget Development Calendar DRAFT 
 
Dr. Pinto, Assistant Superintendent of Finance, provided the Committee with the FY28 Budget 
Development Calendar which is meant to provide a structured timeline for the district’s budgeting 
process, ensuring all tasks are completed efficiently, transparently, and in compliance with 
Massachusetts state laws and local requirements. The following dates have been suggested: 
 
➢ Public Budget Hearing (Regular Meeting, presentation of Budget Book only)  
➢ April 7, 2027, Hold Public Budget Hearing (Tentative TBD, Special Meetings)  
➢ April 10, 2027 (Sat),  
➢ April 16, 2027  
➢ Hold Public Budget Hearing (TBD)/Hearing, Budget Approval (Regular Meeting, if necessary)  
➢ 4th week April 28, 2027, May - June Hearing, Budget Approval (Regular meeting, if necessary) 
May 5, 2027 
 
Mr. Bahou stressed the importance of getting the budget book on time (Friday before the meeting) so 
the Committee has plenty of time to review the budget book before the budget hearing. 
 
Mr. Conway moved to approve the draft budget development calendar; the motion was seconded by 
Mr. Lay. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
8.4. Restraint policy for School Committee Approval 
 
Ms. Brown-LeGrand, Assistant Superintendent for Student Support Services informed the Committee on 
the recommendation of the Staff Counsel from the Office of Student Support Services that the district is 
submitting the attached Policy JKAA, developed by the Massachusetts Association of School Committees 
(MASC): r:12026 in response to updates to the Massachusetts Department of Elementary and Secondary 
Education (DESE) regulations under 603 CMR 46.00. The revised regulations make significant changes to 
the definitions, requirements, and use of time-out rooms, seclusion, and physical restraint, as well as 
establishing enhanced requirements for the collection and submission of data regarding the use of 
seclusion and physical restraint to DESE. The recommendation is for the Committee to vote to adopt 
Policy JKAA, which comprehensively addresses the applicable statutes and regulations governing the use 
of time-out, seclusion, and physical restraint with students. Adoption of this policy will provide a clear 
and consistent framework for the district and ensure alignment with current state requirements. 
 
Mr. Conway moved to approve the Restraint Policy (JKAA); the motion was seconded by Mr. Bahou. 
The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
Mr. Bahou moved to rescind existing policy JKA-R; the motion was seconded by Ms. McFadden. The 
motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin).
(Page 7 of 7) 
 
Lowell Public Schools • 155 Merrimack Street • Lowell, MA 01852 • http://www.lowell.k12.ma.us 
 
 
 
9. CONVENTION/CONFERENCE REQUESTS 
 
9.1. Overnight Out of State Travel Request - National Association for the Education of Homeless Youth 
 
Mr. Bahou requested a report be provided to the Committee regarding this trip. 
 
Ms. Delrossi moved to approve the convention/conference request; the motion was seconded by Ms. 
McFadden. The motion passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
10. PROFESSIONAL PERSONNEL 
 
10.1. The members of the Lowell School Administrator Association (LSAA) hereby request twenty-eight 
[28] sick days to Sheela Pyles, School Psychologist. 
 
This agenda item was withdrawn. 
 
11. ADJOURNMENT 
 
Mr. Conway moved to adjourn at 8:09 p.m.; the motion was seconded by Mr. Bahou. The motion 
passed with 6 yeas, 1 absent (Ms. Martin). 
 
Respectfully submitted, 
 
Liam Skinner, Superintendent and 
Secretary to the Lowell School Committee
